title: Month intervals land on the same day; a missing day rolls back
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. These are number and date accuracy cases: enter the exact inputs, read the value the screen shows, and compare it with the value worked out below.
  3. A schedule "Date check" with services "M1" (calendar Every 1 month) and "D90" (calendar Every 90 days) and "M3" (Every 3 months); four test assets enrolled on it.
  4. Record completions with the asset's Maintenance tab row menu > Mark complete > Completed elsewhere > Reset date (a Reset date can be any past date).
custom_steps:
1. Asset 1: Mark complete M1 with Reset date 15 Jan 2026; read M1's Due cell.
  2. Asset 2: Mark complete M1 with Reset date 31 Jan 2026; read M1's Due cell.
  3. Asset 3: Mark complete M1 with Reset date 31 Jan 2024 (a leap year); read M1's Due cell.
  4. Asset 4: Mark complete D90 and M3, both with Reset date 1 Nov 2025; read both Due cells.
  5. Find assets 1 to 4 on the worklist (all overdue) and compare their Due cells with the asset tab.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Asset 1: "Feb 2026 · Calendar" (15 Jan + 1 month = 15 Feb 2026), badge Overdue.
  • Asset 2: "Feb 2026 · Calendar" (31 Jan + 1 month: 31 Feb does not exist, so 28 Feb 2026), not Mar 2026.
  • Asset 3: "Feb 2024 · Calendar" (31 Jan 2024 + 1 month = 29 Feb 2024, the last day of February), not Mar 2024.
  • Asset 4: D90 reads "Jan 2026 · Calendar" (1 Nov 2025 + 90 days = 30 Jan 2026) while M3 reads "Feb 2026 · Calendar" (1 Nov 2025 + 3 months = 1 Feb 2026): days drift against the calendar, months keep the day.
  • The worklist shows the same months as the asset tab.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S2 (How the next date is worked out; S2-R14, S2-E5; S11-R13 copied from Chunk 2; S18-R3); read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R14: “A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month, counted from the last completion, and produces a specific date rather than a month”
  • S2-E5: “Where the anchor day does not exist in the target month, the date falls on that month's last day. A service completed on 31 January and set to one month comes due 28 February”
  • S11-R13: “A date from the calendar reads its month and Calendar”
  • S2-R14: “A days interval counts days and drifts relative to the calendar, which is what a shop choosing days is asking for”
  • S18-R3: “Reset date is always shown and is never in the future”
